newsitem.title: FINLAND: ETLA CUTS 1997 3-MTH HELIBOR FORECAST TO 3.0 PCT.
newsitem.headline: ETLA CUTS 1997 3-MTH HELIBOR FORECAST TO 3.0 PCT.

text.p: The Research Institute of the Finnish Economy (ETLA) said it expected German monetary policy to remain lax in 1997, and it cut its forecast for Finnish three-month interest rates to 3.0 percent next year.
"After the ERM entry interest rates in Finland will depend increasingly upon monetary policy practiced in the core EU countries," ETLA said in a monthly report received on Tuesday.
"German monetary policy will remain lax next year as fiscal policy is kept tight to ensure fulfilment of the EMU criteria," ETLA said.

"The forecast for the three-month Helibor rates for next year has been revised downwards by half a percentage point to three percent," it said, adding it had also lowered its forecasts for bond yields.
"Ten-year bond yields are expected to remain next year below the 7.1 percent average of this year," ETLA said.
The three-month Helibor interest rate closed at 3.09 percent on Tuesday and the 10-year governmemt bond yield closed at 6.21 percent.
A tightening of monetary policy in Europe was expected to start at the earliest toward the end of 1997 "when economic growth picks up momentum," ETLA said.
In Finland, inflation expectations would "depend greatly" on the late autumn 1997 talks for wage settlements due to take effect in February 1998, the institute said.
ETLA recalled that prior to the last round of pay talks in the autumn of 1995, the Bank of Finland had hiked the tender rate as a warning signal.
"This time around it is hoped that cool heads will prevail in the central bank as well as the labour unions and employer organisations," ETLA said.
